title: Hygiene & disease prevention
examples: If I get sick, is it always because of germs?
What is the best way to keep my hands clean?
Do I need to get shots to stay healthy?

explain.say: Today we will learn about keeping ourselves healthy.
First we learn about washing our hands properly.

items: Lather with soap for twenty seconds

explain.say: Next we learn about vaccines and how they help us.
Washing hands removes germs that can make us sick.
Vaccines teach your body to fight off bad germs early.
In real life, washing hands before eating is very important.

faq.q: How long should I wash my hands for?
faq.a: You should wash your hands for about twenty seconds. This is about as long as singing 'happy birthday' twice.
asks: What is the time for washing hands?

faq.q: Do vaccines give you the actual sickness?
faq.a: No, vaccines only use parts of germs that are safe. They teach your body how to fight the real germ later.

faq.q: What are the best times to wash my hands?
faq.a: You should wash them after using the bathroom and before touching food. These are two very important times.
asks: When should I wash my hands?

faq.q: Can I just use hand sanitizer instead of soap and water?
faq.a: Hand sanitizer is okay sometimes, but soap and water are best because they wash away dirt and germs too. Always wash when you can.
asks: When is soap better than sanitizer?

faq.q: Does getting vaccinated mean I will never get sick?
faq.a: No, vaccines help you fight off specific diseases. They make you much less likely to get very sick from them.
asks: Are vaccines a guarantee against sickness?
Will I never get sick after a shot?

facts: Soap and water physically wash away germs from your skin.
Vaccines introduce safe parts of germs to train your immune system.
Washing hands is very important before preparing or eating food.
The immune system fights off germs when it detects them.

quiz.say: What is the main purpose of washing hands?
quiz.why: Soap and water physically wash away germs from your skin.

wrong.1: While soap can smell nice, its main job is cleaning.
wrong.2: Drying is the last step; the cleaning is the main goal.
wrong.3: Shiny hands do not mean they are clean of germs.

quiz.say: What do vaccines help your body do?

options.show: Make you forget how to fight germs.
options.say: Make you forget how to fight germs.

options.show: Prevent all kinds of germs forever.
options.say: Prevent all kinds of germs forever.

quiz.why: Vaccines introduce safe parts of germs to train your immune system.

wrong.0: Immunity takes time and training from the vaccine.
wrong.1: Vaccines teach your body, they do not weaken it.
wrong.3: Vaccines only protect against specific diseases.

quiz.say: If you touch a surface and then eat a snack, what should you do?

options.show: Blow nose on hand and eat.
options.say: Blow nose on hand and eat.

quiz.why: Washing hands first removes germs from surfaces you touched.

wrong.0: Clothes can trap and spread germs, not remove them.
wrong.1: Nose tissues carry germs that should not touch food.
wrong.2: Soap and water are better because they remove dirt too.
